jsonld.name: White-label SEO
jsonld.description: White-label SEO delivered by MMC for agencies, studios and consultancies, under the agency's own brand.

acceptedAnswer.text: It is SEO work done by a provider and sold by your agency under its own brand. MMC does the audit, fixes, content and reporting; you keep the client, the pricing and the relationship.
Audit, technical fixes, on-page work, keyword mapping, content briefs, local SEO and reporting. We scope exactly which pieces your client needs and write it down.

mainEntity.name: How much does white-label SEO cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the site, the market and the work in scope, so we price each scope in writing rather than publish a rate card. Invoices are in Indian rupees or US dollars, and the minimum commitment is three months. Our pricing models page explains the cost drivers.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with UK, US, Canadian and Australian agencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do, along with agencies in the UAE, Singapore, India and the rest of Europe. UK and Australian agencies get full overlap with our working day; US and Canadian agencies get overlap in the evening, India time, or a dedicated shift. Exact hours are agreed per team.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle local SEO and Google Business Profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do, for businesses in the US and the UK: Google Business Profile management, citations, review flows and location pages, reported under your brand.

mainEntity.name: Can I sell your SEO audit as my own product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The audit can carry your branding and be sold on its own or used as the start of a retainer.

mainEntity.name: Do you do link building too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as a separate service. See our white-label link building page for how outreach and placements are handled.

mainEntity.name: Can you promise rankings for my client?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and you should not either. Rankings depend on many factors. We commit to the work in the scope and report what moves.

mainEntity.name: Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

mainEntity.name: How do we get started with white-label SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start with the client's site, analytics and search console access, sign the NDA and run an audit. You then get a plan to present.

blocks.h: White-label SEO for agencies: outsourced, under your name
paras: Agencies search for this under several names: white-label SEO, outsourced SEO, SEO fulfilment or private-label SEO. They describe the same arrangement. A white-label SEO provider does the hands-on work, and your agency sells it, presents it and invoices for it as its own.
If you would rather sell fixed SEO packages at a wholesale rate, see the SEO reseller programme. This page covers delivery: what we do each month and how it reaches your client under your brand.

blocks.h: A white-label SEO month, step by step
paras: Audit. Work starts with a crawl, technical and content audit written up in your template, with a ranked fix list you can present or sell on its own.
Technical fixes. Indexing, speed, site structure, internal links and schema, shipped in batches you approve, or handed to the client's developers as clear tickets.
On-page and content. Titles, headings and page copy aligned to search intent, plus content briefs and edits for the pages that matter most to the client.
Links. Editorial outreach and digital PR, run as a separate service with no paid link networks. See white-label link building.

blocks.h: Local SEO for US and UK businesses
paras: We run local SEO for your clients' businesses in the US and the UK, including those with several locations.
Google Business Profile. Categories, services, products, photos and posts kept accurate for each location, through access the client grants.

Citations and reviews. Business name, address and phone kept consistent across the main directories and data sources in each country, and a review request flow your client can run, with replies drafted for your approval.
Location pages. One useful page per location, with local detail rather than a copied template, linked into the site's structure.
As with the rest of SEO, nobody can promise map positions. We report the work done and what changed.

Each month you get a report in your format: work done, rankings, organic traffic and enquiries, with a short note you can read out on the client call. It can go out from your domain under your logo. See white-label reporting.

blocks.h: What white-label SEO costs and why
paras: We do not publish prices, because the same label covers very different work. The cost moves with the size and technical state of the site, how competitive the client's market is, how much content is in scope each month, the number of locations for local SEO, whether link building is included and how detailed the reporting needs to be.
Every scope is written down and invoiced in Indian rupees or US dollars, with a minimum commitment of three months. The pricing models page explains how to set your margin on top.

blocks.h: Delivered from India, run to your hours
paras: Our SEO team works from India. Agencies in the UK, Australia, the UAE and Singapore get full overlap with our working day. US agencies get partial overlap in the evening, India time, or a dedicated shift for a team that needs more. Written updates arrive at fixed times each day wherever you are, and exact hours are agreed per team.
More on how this works: white-label delivery from India.

blocks.h: How to choose a white-label SEO provider
paras: Before you sign with any provider, including us, check these.
An NDA and a no-contact rule in writing, before you share client details.
Account ownership. Search Console, analytics and the CMS stay in your client's name; the provider gets access, not ownership.
A written scope that says what is done each month and what is not.
A pilot on one client before you commit more.
Link methods stated plainly, with no paid link networks or private blog networks.
Sample work. Ask to see an audit and a report. We can show an anonymised sample audit on the call.
No promised rankings. A provider that promises positions is guessing.

cta.lede: On a call, with a senior strategist. We scope your first SEO client and agree how we work behind you.

stages.breaks: Access arrives late, so the audit starts blind.
stages.why: Without Search Console and CMS access, findings are guesses and the fix list slips past the client call.
stages.does: One access checklist goes out at the start, and we log what is missing so the audit scope stays honest.

stages.breaks: Keywords are mapped to pages nobody agreed.
stages.why: If you and the client have not signed off the map, every later page is open to argument.
stages.does: We group searches by intent, map each to a page and send the map for your approval before any writing.

stages.breaks: Thin pages ship to hit the deadline.
stages.why: A rushed page with nothing new on it will not rank, and the client blames the agency.
stages.does: Briefs say what each page must add, and a second editor checks it against the brief before it reaches you.

stages.breaks: Pages bury the answer the buyer came for.
stages.why: Search results and AI answers favour pages that reply first and explain after.
stages.does: Priority pages are reopened with a direct answer, then detail, FAQs and matching structured data.

stages.why: A traffic chart does not tell the client whether SEO paid for itself.
stages.does: Your report pairs rankings and traffic with enquiries from the client's own analytics, plus a plain next-steps note.
